editorial.headline: Paint Retail: Nationally Open, Barred to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Retail trade in construction paints is nationally open to foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for the activity today.
editorial.body:
This activity is the retail sale of paints, varnishes, lacquers and other construction coatings. Its practical territory runs from primers and metal, wood and wall paints to enamel, putty, filler, varnish and lacquer. It is a trade activity centred on the materials that finish, protect and prepare built surfaces—not merely on paint as a single product category. The stated scope also includes direct sales, giving the activity a clear retail character across the coating range.

Nationally, the position is open. Foreign ownership may reach 100%, under the national PMA position recorded for this activity. The activity is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because it describes a retail activity available across the full scale range, rather than one confined by the record to a particular size of enterprise. The national opening is recorded with Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 as its source.

Bali changes the result decisively for PMA registration. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, bringing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. The relevant Bali status is Blocked (risk class): the restriction arises from the activity’s risk classification at that scale, not from any reduction in the national foreign-ownership ceiling.

This is therefore a case where the national and Bali answers must be kept distinct. The national record permits up to full foreign ownership; Bali’s provincial moratorium nonetheless blocks PMA registration for the activity. The Bali restriction is recorded as taking effect in May 2026, with Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP identified as the source. For founders, the useful reading is exact rather than optimistic: the activity remains nationally open, but that national openness does not produce a PMA registration route in Bali while the stated moratorium applies.
